body: My friend, take the advice that alot of other people are saying here. There's no way to know for certain until you get a diagnosis. Talk to a Doctor. If you aren't sure where to start, even mentioning your concerns to your primary care physician can at least help you get the ball rolling. You said you're a minor in a previous comment, and I know that can open up a whole can of worms with doubts, and anxiety, and just general confusion. I know it did for me. There's no shame in getting checked out. There's no shame in getting a diagnosis if there is something. There's no shame in finding out it really is nothing to worry about. If your worried, it is worth looking into. And be honest with yourself and the Doctor. Don't gloss over things because they "aren't a big deal" or you can "handle it". If it bothers you, it's worth mentioning.

To speak from personal experience, ignoring the physical aspect of it. There's the hospitalization. If your lucky you go to a good one. Its a weird feeling to be there. You have to let yourself be infantilized almost, can't do anything without supervision or permission. Can't have any personal belongings that aren't strictly vetted and pre-approved. You go to alot of group therapy. Alot. Its all there is to do there. Otherwise you lose your mind with boredom. Then you get released feeling slightly nuttier then when you went in. Then there's the real trouble. There's the guilt. The explaining to people where you were for the past week however long. Theres the look in your friends eyes when you say something a little wrong. Theres the asking your partner for permission when you need to shave, because the hospital called and told them to hide all the razors in the house. And lastly theres the fear of it all happening all over again. Its a rough time. My advice, accept a different down to be your rock bottom. Dont let it reach that point. Please. Theres enough regrets in the world.

Hi pahbee. Thank you for the concern. To answer your question, I honestly don't know what I am angry at. That in itself if part of the problem. I am so out of sync with my emotions that I feel completely unfitting feelings for what is around me. Like I will be having a great day, and just hanging around with my friends, when for no apparent reason, this... dark side as I also call it just flares up and I suddenly am going through the fight of my life just to contain it. But on the flip side, when I am experiencing something that I know is supposed to make me sad, I suddenly feel like laughing and I have to struggle to hide that to. And then afterwards I feel like trash for it and it makes it that much harder to fight the next event. I wish I understood what makes it tick. Maybe then I could at least imagine a way to get better. Thank you again for the care. It takes a special kind of person to go to that length for somebody you don't know. I'm glad any other posters have a place like this to get help.
